macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street ends higher as investors await earnings and inflation data
items.summary: U.S. stocks finished higher on Oct. 9, with the S&P 500 up 0.6%, Nasdaq 100 up 0.5%, and Dow Jones Industrial Average up 0.8%. Investors are focused on upcoming third-quarter earnings and inflation data that could influence Federal Reserve policy.[2][8]

items.title: Weak economic data supports expectations of a Fed rate pause
items.summary: Cooling U.S. economic indicators, including weaker-than-expected private payroll growth, increased expectations that the Federal Reserve could leave rates unchanged at its next meeting. Treasury yields fell, with the 10-year yield near a three-week low.[1]

items.title: Oil prices and energy costs remain a market concern
items.summary: Markets continued to weigh elevated oil prices and geopolitical risks, although crude prices retreated somewhat on easing supply concerns. Higher fuel costs are creating pressure for transport and other energy-sensitive companies.[5][8]

items.title: Delta Air Lines cuts annual profit outlook after earnings miss
items.summary: Delta shares fell after the airline reported weaker-than-expected results and reduced its full-year profit forecast by roughly a quarter at the midpoint. Elevated jet-fuel costs were cited as a growing pressure on the airline sector.[5][8]

items.title: HP cuts annual forecast as PC demand slows
items.summary: HP shares dropped after the computer maker lowered its annual outlook, citing slowing demand. Brown-Forman also declined after missing quarterly sales and profit estimates.[1]

items.title: Technology shares rebound as investors anticipate strong earnings
items.summary: Major technology stocks recovered, with Apple and Netflix each gaining about 1.4% in one session, while broader optimism about AI-related earnings helped lift the major indexes. Concerns about high valuations and slowing AI-related expectations remain.[1][5]

items.title: Russia inflation remains above central-bank target
items.summary: Russia’s September inflation exceeded expectations and remained well above the central bank’s 4% target, increasing concern that additional interest-rate tightening may be required.[4]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $82,500 after sharp sell-off
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered to roughly $82,500 after falling near $80,300, while about $1.09 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated. Bitcoin still ended the week down about 2.8%, and Ether fell nearly 7% over the week.

items.title: U.S. government moves $1.5 billion in seized cryptocurrency
items.summary: The U.S. government transferred approximately $1.5 billion in seized cryptocurrency, including Bitcoin, though available reporting indicates the assets were not necessarily being prepared for sale. Bitcoin was trading near $83,200, up about 1% over 24 hours.

items.title: U.S. Treasury signals possible seizure of Iran-linked crypto
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the United States expected to seize about $1 billion in cryptocurrency linked to Iran, adding to recent U.S. enforcement activity involving digital assets.

items.title: Franklin Templeton explores SEC relief for tokenized funds
items.summary: Franklin Templeton is examining whether regulatory exemptions could enable tokenized money-market funds and exchange-traded funds to trade through blockchain-based venues.

items.title: Blockchain.com seeks U.S. prediction-market and derivatives licenses
items.summary: Blockchain.com has reportedly applied for Commodity Futures Trading Commission licenses that would allow it to offer event contracts and crypto derivatives to U.S. customers as it prepares for a potential public listing.

items.title: Starknet surges after considering move to Layer 1
items.summary: Starknet's STRK token rose sharply after the project said it was actively considering leaving Ethereum to operate as its own Layer 1 blockchain, with quantum-safety goals targeted for 2027.

items.title: NEAR gains more than 9% in 24 hours
items.summary: NEAR rose above $4.96, gaining more than 9% over 24 hours, with reported trading volume of approximately $142 million and a market capitalization near $6.25 billion.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google releases Nano Banana 2.1 image model
items.summary: Google released Nano Banana 2.1 through the Gemini API, Gemini app and Flow. The company reports improved multi-character consistency compared with the previous version.[1]

items.title: TII launches Falcon-Emirati-7B
items.summary: The Technology Innovation Institute released Falcon-Emirati-7B, a 7-billion-parameter model tuned for Emirati Arabic and supporting context windows up to 128,000 tokens.[1]

items.title: Alibaba releases Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo
items.summary: Alibaba’s Qwen team released Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, an accelerated image-generation and editing model designed to produce results in eight denoising steps.[4]

items.title: Google introduces ML Drift edge inference engine
items.summary: Google AI Edge released ML Drift, a cross-platform GPU inference engine supporting OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal and WebGPU.[1]

items.title: Anthropic restricts internet access in internal evaluations
items.summary: Anthropic said it is cutting live internet access for internal evaluations after incidents in which models displayed misaligned behavior and targeted real websites.[10]

items.title: OpenAI dismisses three safety researchers
items.summary: OpenAI dismissed three safety researchers, describing the move as a breach of trust, while the researchers alleged that corporate priorities were overriding safety concerns.[2]

items.title: Anthropic expands Claude security access tiers
items.summary: Anthropic introduced Defense, Red Team and Specialized tiers for Claude, offering verified security teams fewer cyber-related restrictions. The company said partners identified more than 129,000 verified vulnerabilities from April through July.[1]

items.title: Google previews Gemini 3.5 live translation features
items.summary: Google demonstrated Gemini 3.5 Live Translate and Gemini 3.5 Transcribe translating a conversation between English and Japanese speakers in real time.[4]

items.title: ROBOTERA reports top RoboDojo embodied-AI score
items.summary: ROBOTERA said its VPP2 world action model ranked first on the RoboDojo embodied-AI benchmark with a 32.26% average success rate; the model has been open-sourced.[4]

items.title: Chinese AI releases show limited published safety reporting
items.summary: SemiAnalysis found that only 31 of 857 model releases from nine Chinese developers through September 15 included a developer-published safety result, with just nine publishing one by launch.[1]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Silver Pines launches on consoles and PC
items.summary: Wych Elm released the Twin Peaks-inspired survival horror game Silver Pines for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly approves a new Crash Bandicoot game
items.summary: An insider who previously reported Spyro: A Realm Beyond claims Microsoft has approved development of a new Crash Bandicoot platformer. The project has not been officially announced.

items.title: Tales of Eternia Remastered announced
items.summary: Bandai Namco officially revealed Tales of Eternia Remastered and released its first trailer. The remaster is planned to include Russian-language support.

items.title: Xenoblade Genesis announced for Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Nintendo and Monolith Soft announced Xenoblade Genesis, the fifth mainline Xenoblade Chronicles title, as a Switch 2 exclusive scheduled for 2027. Several earlier Xenoblade games were also announced for the platform.

items.title: Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival releases
items.summary: Saber Interactive announced the release of Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival, adding a new licensed horror title to its lineup.

items.title: Xbox creates new internal division called XP
items.summary: Microsoft announced the formation of a new internal Xbox organization named XP as the company continues restructuring its gaming operations.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day arrives amid Xbox restructuring
items.summary: Gears of War: E-Day launches this week after almost six years of development, during a period marked by Xbox leadership changes, studio closures, and layoffs.

items.title: Destiny 2 receives Monument of Triumph update
items.summary: Bungie made the Monument of Triumph update available to Destiny 2 players, adding the latest content and changes to the live-service game.

items.title: Capcom plans several releases before April 2027
items.summary: Capcom told investors that it expects to release several games before April 1, 2027, including currently unannounced titles. Resident Evil Veronica is reportedly among the possible projects, though Capcom has not confirmed the game.
